newsitem.title: SOMALIA: Gunmen kidnap Somali aid worker, aid officials say.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen kidnap Somali aid worker, aid officials say.

text.p: Gunmen have abducted a Somali doctor with the aid agency CARE International in north Mogadishu, CARE officials said on Saturday.
Saed Aden Mohamed Firdis, head of CARE's Somali Partnership Projects, was abducted late on Friday from outside his house in a part of the city controlled by faction leader Ali Mahdi Mohamed.
But CARE officials in Nairobi denied the abduction was connected to Firdis' work for the organisation and said it was a clan issue.

"They kidnapped him because he is from the Darood clan but he is living in an Abgal area of north Mogadishu. It is much more a clan issue," said Musdaque Ahmed, project manager of CARE Somalia, who returned to Nairobi from Mogadishu on Saturday.
"We will let the clan elders work on this problem. This is a clan issue and nothing to do with CARE," said Ahmed by telephone. He added he expected Firdis's release this weekend.
The abduction coincided with the return to north Mogadishu on Friday of religious leader Sheikh Ali Dhere backed by 30 "technical" battlewagons, witnesses said.
Dhere, formerly chairman of north Mogadishu's Islamic courts, told hundreds of cheering supporters that Islamic sharia law should be restored.
He left Somalia for Saudi Arabia in May after a series of armed confrontations with Ali Mahdi Mohamed but was reinstated after mediation by clan elders.
Somalia has been without central government since dictator Mohamed Siad Barre was ousted in 1991. The Horn of Africa country suffered famine and civil war in 1992/3 but is now largely at peace.
